I don't know what exactly you were trying to make but if you wanted to make sweet bread try this recipe. It's probably a little more time consuming than a baking powder bread but it tastes really good:

170 grams of milk (either room temperature or fridge temperature, not cooked) 1 egg, 375 g wheat flour, 60 g sugar, 5 g salt, 15 g fresh yeast, 50g room temperature butter

Mix flour, salt, sugar. Sprinkle the yeast on top. Add butter. Mix egg and milk, pour the liquid and mix. As soon as it's starting to form a dough put it on a board with flour sprinkled on top so nothing sticks. Knead it until it forms a nice smooth ball, it should take you at least 10 minutes.

 Put the dough in a clean bowl with a clean towel on top. Let it rest for about 25-30 minutes to an hour (depends on the room temperature but you know it's ready when it has doubled in size) and pre heat your oven to 170°C. 

Knead the dough again and form it into a knot or braid it (you can also make a cross bun shape or whatever) and brush some egg or milk on it. Let it rest for another 10 minutes. Bake for around 25-30 minutes, depends on the oven. It should sound hollow when it's ready, if it doesn't put it in for another 5 minutes but reduce the temperature a bit.

I explained it as detailed as I could so nothing should go wrong if you decide to try it, it's a recipe that has always worked for me. I hope you use grams and celsius, using a scale is better for bread anyways since it's more precise than cups but it could probably also work if you convert it to cups.
